Bachelor of Business
description:
TAFE Queensland's Bachelor of Business runs through the same University of Canberra partnership arrangement that underpins its creative-industries degrees, giving students access to a metropolitan business curriculum without leaving Brisbane's South Bank, Mt Gravatt or Coomera campuses. Class sizes are smaller than at a standard university business school, and a lot of the assessment is built around applied projects with real local businesses rather than case studies written for a textbook.

The core is conventional business fundamentals: accounting, marketing, management, economics and business law, but students choose a major partway through, with options that track Queensland's actual employment mix: management, marketing, human resource management and event/tourism-adjacent majors show up more than a generic finance-only track would. Because the degree sits inside a TAFE campus rather than a university one, students doing a business major alongside, say, a hospitality or IT diploma at the same site can cross-enrol in electives from those areas, which isn't something a standalone university business degree typically allows.

Graduates go into generalist business, management-trainee, marketing coordinator and small-business roles across Queensland, and the degree also functions as a credentialing step for TAFE Queensland students moving up from a business-related diploma.
curriculum:
Year 1: Accounting Principles, Introduction to Management, Marketing Fundamentals, Business Economics, Business Law, Business Communication
Year 2: Organisational Behaviour, Financial Management, major-specific units begin (Management, Marketing or Human Resource Management stream), Business Analytics, Business Ethics and Sustainability
Year 3: Strategic Management, major capstone units, Applied Business Project (client-based consulting project), electives from cross-campus TAFE Queensland offerings
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Creative Industries (Drama and Performance)
description:
Run out of TAFE Queensland's South Bank campus in partnership with the University of Canberra, this degree trains performers alongside the people who will end up producing, facilitating and managing the work around them. The course explicitly covers the role of arts facilitators, educators, producers and project managers in creating socially engaged performance work, not just acting technique.

It's built to take students at very different starting points: TAFE Queensland describes it as suited to complete beginners as much as emerging or already-working performers who want to formalise their practice, sit alongside performance theory and pick up professional and entrepreneurial skills they may not have needed for community or amateur work. South Bank's location gives the cohort proximity to Brisbane's professional theatre scene, and the course draws on that for industry contact and, per TAFE Queensland's own program materials, an active on-campus theatre community.

It's a three-year, Commonwealth Supported Place degree with entry based on an entrance rank and typical alternate pathway and admission scheme options. Graduates move into performance work, but the producer/facilitator strand of the curriculum also opens out into arts administration, community arts and theatre-in-education roles that a pure acting degree wouldn't prepare students for as directly.
curriculum:
Year 1: Performance Foundations, Voice and Movement, Introduction to Devising, Theatre History and Theory, Ensemble Practice
Year 2: Text-Based Performance, Physical Theatre, Performance for Social Change, Arts Facilitation and Community Practice, production placement
Year 3: Directing and Dramaturgy, Producing and Project Management for the Arts, Entrepreneurship for Performing Artists, capstone performance season (devised or directed public production)
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent); audition/interview may be requested

name: Bachelor of Creative Industries (Visual Arts)
description:
Like the Visual Communication Design degree, this is a combined qualification: a TAFE Queensland Diploma of Visual Arts feeds into the University of Canberra's Bachelor of Creative Industries (Visual Arts) award. The structure suits students who aren't certain yet whether they want a strictly technical art practice or a broader creative-industries career, since the diploma phase is studio-heavy and the degree phase opens out into curating, arts administration and public art.

Studio practice spans drawing, painting, sculpture, printmaking and increasingly digital and mixed media, with the later degree units pushing students toward professional contexts such as exhibition planning, artist statements, grant writing, and gallery relationships that a purely technical diploma wouldn't cover. Brisbane's South Bank campus sits a short walk from the Queensland Art Gallery and GOMA, and the course leans on that proximity for guest critiques and exhibition opportunities rather than treating it as incidental.

Career outcomes are deliberately broad: gallery and museum work, arts education, arts administration, curating, exhibition and display design and public art commissions all show up as destinations, which reflects the creative-industries framing more than a narrower "fine artist" pathway would.
curriculum:
Diploma phase: Drawing and Visual Language, Painting Studio, Printmaking, Sculpture and 3D Practice, Materials and Processes, diploma exhibition project
Degree phase (University of Canberra): Contemporary Art Theory, Curatorial Practice, Arts Administration and Grant Writing, Exhibition and Display Design, Professional Studio Practice, capstone body of work and public exhibition
Credit pathway: TAFE Queensland diploma credit transfers up to 24 credit points into the bachelor's
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent); folio may be requested

name: Bachelor of Dental Prosthetics
description:
This AQF Level 7 degree is accredited by the Australian Dental Council and approved by the Dental Board of Australia, and it trains one of the few allied dental professions that can treat patients directly rather than only supporting a dentist. Dental prosthetists issue, maintain and examine dentures, insert and try in prosthetics, take impressions and carry out the technical laboratory work themselves, a scope of practice that's genuinely unusual in dentistry, where most non-dentist roles are lab-only or chairside-assist-only.

Coursework covers not just full and partial dentures but more specialised appliances: sleep apnoea and anti-snoring devices, splints, and immediate dentures fitted the same day as extractions. Training happens in TAFE Queensland's working denture clinic, where students treat real patients under supervision using the same lab equipment they'll use professionally, rather than working exclusively on models.

The entry requirement that gets flagged repeatedly by TAFE Queensland itself is manual dexterity: it's assessed at admission and has to be maintained throughout enrolment, which says something about how hands-on the daily work actually is. Graduates are eligible to register as dental prosthetists with the Dental Board of Australia and can go into private practice, dental laboratories or continue into further postgraduate dental study.
curriculum:
Year 1: Oral Anatomy and Physiology, Dental Materials Science, Introduction to Denture Construction, Infection Control and Clinical Practice, Impression Taking and Casting
Year 2: Complete Denture Prosthetics, Partial Denture Design, Occlusion and Articulation, Clinical Practice I (working denture clinic, supervised patient treatment)
Year 3: Immediate Dentures and Same-Day Prosthetics, Sleep Apnoea and Splint Devices, Removable Prosthodontic Complications, Clinical Practice II, Professional and Regulatory Practice for Dental Prosthetists
Clinical training: supervised patient treatment throughout in TAFE Queensland's on-site working denture clinic and dental laboratory
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent) plus relevant work placement component; accredited by the Australian Dental Council

name: Bachelor of Design (Visual Communication Design)
description:
Delivered by TAFE Queensland in partnership with the University of Canberra, this is a dual-award structure: students complete a TAFE Queensland Diploma of Graphic Design en route to the University of Canberra's Bachelor of Digital Design (Visual Communication Design) testamur, which is the actual degree name that appears on the parchment despite the program being commonly listed under the broader title. The arrangement means students get a vocational, portfolio-heavy first phase before the degree work broadens into strategy and theory.

Studio work covers typography, logotype and identity design, publication layout, packaging, environmental graphics and digital design, taught by working designers rather than exclusively by academic staff. Class sizes at the South Bank and Coomera studios are kept small enough that students get direct one-on-one critique, which matters in a discipline where the difference between a portfolio that gets a graduate an interview and one that doesn't often comes down to individual feedback rather than course content.

Graduates leave with an industry-ready portfolio and typically move into junior graphic design, brand identity, digital design or in-house studio roles; the credit-transfer arrangement (any one-year TAFE Queensland diploma articulates with 24 credit points, equivalent to a full year of the bachelor's) also makes this a common re-entry point for students who started a diploma elsewhere and want to upgrade to a degree.
curriculum:
Diploma phase: Design Fundamentals, Typography 1 & 2, Digital Imaging, Layout and Publication Design, Branding and Identity, Packaging Design, industry-based diploma project
Degree phase (University of Canberra): Design Theory and Criticism, Environmental and Wayfinding Design, Interactive and Motion Design, Design for Social Impact, Professional Practice, capstone design project and portfolio exhibition
Credit pathway: completed TAFE Queensland diplomas can transfer up to 24 credit points (one year) into the bachelor's component
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent); delivered in partnership with the University of Canberra

name: Bachelor of Information Technology (Cyber Security)
description:
This degree sits inside TAFE Queensland's broader IT offering at the Coomera campus, where students share lab space (the IT, Immersive Technology and Cyber Security Labs) with games design and network engineering cohorts rather than working in isolation. That cross-pollination matters more than it sounds: a lot of the practical cyber security work students end up doing (penetration testing a web app, hardening a small business network) touches the same infrastructure other students are building.

The course covers programming, networking and database management before narrowing into security-specific work: threat modelling, intrusion detection, digital forensics and governance frameworks. Queensland's cyber security workforce shortfall is cited constantly in TAFE Queensland's own marketing for this course, and it isn't exaggerated. Demand spans banking, healthcare, retail, defence contractors and state government simultaneously, which gives graduates more geographic flexibility within Queensland than a narrower specialisation would.

Graduates typically land entry-level security analyst, SOC analyst or junior penetration tester roles, and the degree articulates directly into TAFE Queensland's Graduate Diploma and Master of Cyber Security for anyone who wants to keep going.
curriculum:
Year 1: Programming Fundamentals, Network Fundamentals, Database Design and Management, IT Systems and Infrastructure, Introduction to Cyber Security, Professional Practice in IT
Year 2: Network Security and Defence, Operating Systems Security, Web Application Development and Security, Ethical Hacking Fundamentals, Cloud Computing, Systems Analysis and Design
Year 3: Digital Forensics, Cyber Security Governance and Risk, Incident Response and Threat Intelligence, Secure Software Development, capstone industry project (client-based security assessment), electives in IoT security or cryptography
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Nursing
description:
TAFE Queensland's Bachelor of Nursing is built around clinical hours rather than lecture hours. The course schedules 840 hours of Professional Experience Placement across the three years, which clears the 800-hour minimum the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia sets for registration eligibility, and placement blocks are threaded through every year of study instead of stacked at the end.

Before students set foot in a ward, they work through scenarios in TAFE Queensland's simulated hospital wards, which run mock handovers, deteriorating-patient drills and medication rounds under the same documentation standards used in Queensland Health facilities. The course markets itself as "designed by nurses for nurses," and the teaching staff are practising or recently practising RNs rather than career academics, which shows up in how much time is spent on the unglamorous procedural detail of real ward work.

Graduates are eligible to apply for registration as a Registered Nurse with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia (subject to AHPRA requirements) and typically move into acute care, aged care, community health or mental health settings across the Queensland public and private hospital systems.
curriculum:
Year 1: Foundations of Nursing Practice, Anatomy and Physiology A & B, Introduction to Health Assessment, Psychology for Health Professionals, Professional Communication in Health, first Professional Experience Placement block (aged care/sub-acute)
Year 2: Pathophysiology and Pharmacology, Acute Care Nursing, Mental Health Nursing, Nursing Older Persons, Primary Health Care, Research and Evidence-Based Practice, second and third PEP blocks (medical/surgical wards)
Year 3: Complex Care Nursing, Perioperative and Critical Care Nursing, Child and Family Health, Leadership and Transition to Professional Practice, one elective unit, final PEP blocks including a graduate transition placement
Clinical placement: 840 hours total across acute, sub-acute, mental health, community and aged care settings, exceeding the 800-hour AHPRA/NMBA minimum
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent, plus health/immunisation checks (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 overall (typical registration-body bar for nursing programs, approximate)

name: Bachelor of the Built Environment (Architecture)
description:
Delivered with the University of Canberra, this degree is part of an Architects Accreditation Council of Australia-accredited pathway that continues into the Master of Architecture, meaning it's structured from year one as the first half of a longer registration pathway rather than a terminal qualification, which matters for students weighing it against a straight university architecture degree.

Work-integrated learning is built into every stage rather than bolted on as a single placement unit: TAFE Queensland promotes a series of "live" projects run with practising architects and design firms, plus internship placements at local, national and international practices. Studio culture leans into critique from working professionals rather than purely academic staff, and coursework is framed around developing "informed critique" of architecture as both creative and professional practice. The ethical and environmental responsibilities of the profession get explicit attention alongside design skill.

Entry is based on entrance rank, and it's a Commonwealth Supported Place, which keeps the cost profile closer to a standard university architecture degree than to a private design school. Graduates continue to the Master of Architecture for registration eligibility, or move into design, drafting and project roles in the built environment sector without completing the full registration pathway.
curriculum:
Year 1: Architectural Design Studio 1 & 2, History and Theory of Architecture, Construction Technology 1, Digital Representation and CAD, Environmental Design Principles
Year 2: Architectural Design Studio 3 & 4, Structures and Materials, Construction Technology 2, Urban Design and Context, live industry project 1
Year 3: Architectural Design Studio 5 & 6, Professional Practice and Ethics, Sustainable Design, live industry project 2, internship placement, portfolio for progression to Master of Architecture
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent); accredited by the Architects Accreditation Council of Australia

Graduate Diploma in Cyber Security
description:
This is TAFE Queensland's bridging qualification for people who already have IT or related experience but need a formal, accredited cyber security credential fast, and its own marketing is explicit that the intended endpoint is the Master of Cyber Security (Advanced), with graduates able to fast-track straight in rather than starting a master's from scratch. As a standalone qualification it also stands on its own for anyone not planning to continue to postgraduate level.

Content splits fairly evenly between technical security work (system security, digital forensics, ethical hacking and defensive techniques) and governance: cyber policy, compliance and organisational risk. That combination is deliberate; TAFE Queensland is explicit that the course is meant to produce people who understand both the attack surface and the regulatory environment around it, rather than pure penetration testers.

Entry accepts a relevant AQF 5 qualification plus two years' relevant work experience, a relevant bachelor's degree completed within six years, or three years of directly relevant work experience with no formal qualification, which makes this a realistic option for experienced IT staff without a cyber-specific degree.
curriculum:
Core units: System Security and Hardening, Digital Forensics Fundamentals, Ethical Hacking and Penetration Testing, Cyber Policy and Governance, Risk Management and Compliance, Network Defence Techniques
Capstone: applied security assessment project
Progression: graduates can fast-track into the Master of Cyber Security (Advanced) with credit for equivalent units
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree in any discipline (or relevant industry experience considered)

name: Master of Cyber Security
description:
TAFE Queensland pitches this degree specifically at people who don't want to choose between the technical and policy sides of cyber security. The course is built to produce graduates who can both run an incident response and sit across the table from a board explaining what happened and why the organisation's governance failed. That dual framing is unusual for a technical postgraduate degree in this space, where most competitors lean hard into one side or the other.

Entry is flexible by design: applicants can come in via a relevant AQF 5 qualification plus two years' work experience, a relevant bachelor's degree, or three years of straight industry experience with no formal cyber credential at all, which makes it a realistic upgrade path for IT professionals who moved into security informally. Students who complete the Graduate Diploma in Cyber Security first (offered at the same campus) can fast-track directly into this Master's, and TAFE Queensland also runs a "Master of Cyber Security (Advanced)" variant with an extended research or industry project component for those wanting a deeper technical specialisation.

The course leans on Queensland's acute cyber workforce shortage (the state's banking, health, legal, retail, defence and government sectors are all short-staffed at once), and graduates move into security architecture, GRC (governance, risk and compliance), and senior analyst roles rather than purely entry-level positions given the postgraduate entry bar.
curriculum:
Core: Advanced Network Security, Cyber Security Policy and Governance, Digital Forensics and Incident Response, Security Risk Management, Applied Cryptography, Cyber Law and Ethics
Advanced/capstone stream: Enterprise Security Architecture, Threat Intelligence and Analytics, industry-based capstone project (real client security assessment or research thesis for the Advanced stream)
Delivery: coursework plus an industry-linked capstone; fast-track entry available for Graduate Diploma in Cyber Security completers, who receive credit for foundational units
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree in IT or a related discipline (or relevant industry experience considered)
